entries.title: Psalms 77:1
segments:
PSALM LXXVII. 
 
  The psalmist complains of deep distress, and temptations to despair,   ver. 1-10.   He encourages himself to hope, by the remembrance of what God had done   formerly, ver. 11-20.   To the chief musician, to Jeduthun, A psalm of Asaph.

entries.title: Psalms 77:2
segments: V. 2. Night-Which to others was a time of rest and quietness.

entries.title: Psalms 77:3
segments: V. 3. Troubled-Yea, the thoughts of God were now a matter of trouble, because he was angry with me.  Overwhelmed-So far was I from finding relief.

entries.title: Psalms 77:5
segments: V. 5. The days-The mighty works of God in former times.

entries.title: Psalms 77:6
segments: V. 6. My song-The mercies of God vouchsafed to me, and to his people, which have obliged me to sing his praises, not only in the day, but also by night.

entries.title: Psalms 77:10
segments: V. 10. I said-These suspicions of God's faithfulness proceed from the weakness of my faith.  The years-The years wherein God hath done great and glorious works, which are often ascribed to God's right-hand.

entries.title: Psalms 77:13
segments: V. 13. In holiness-God is holy and just, and true in all his works.

entries.title: Psalms 77:16
segments: V. 16. Afraid-And stood still, as men astonished, do.

entries.title: Psalms 77:17
segments: V. 17. Poured-When the Israelites passed over the sea. Arrows-Hail-stones or lightnings.

entries.title: Psalms 77:19
segments: V. 19. Not known-Because the water returned and covered them.

entries.title: Psalms 77:20
segments: V. 20. Leddest-First through the sea, and afterwards through the wilderness, with singular care and tenderness, as a shepherd doth his sheep.
